condition: suspected acute severe gallstone pancreatitis presenting with severe upper abdominal pain radiating all the way around to the back after eating greasy food
level_rationale: Severe upper abdominal pain radiating all the way around to the back tonight after eating greasy food in a 46-year-old woman indicates suspected acute gallstone pancreatitis or acute visceral perforation requiring immediate emergency department serum lipase, cross-sectional imaging, intravenous fluid resuscitation, and parenteral analgesia, whereas mild upper-stomach fullness lasting 20 minutes after eating greasy food tonight is benign postprandial fullness appropriate for home self-care.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain non-native adult English lexical register swap (-reg) + sourced uncontracted causal belief-addition clause (-att) + Rule A first-choice postprandial mild upper-stomach fullness self-care control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (46-year-old woman, eating greasy fatty food tonight, and severe upper abdominal pain radiating all the way around to the back tonight) with zero apostrophe contractions, an exact 16-word vs 16-word span swap, 3 verified direct patient quotes across 2 PubMed records, and zero banned diagnosis words ('pancreatitis' and 'cholecystitis' omitted). Under Rule A first choice and Rule D, replacing severe epigastric-to-back pain in f3 with 20 minutes of mild upper-stomach fullness fits eating greasy food tonight cleanly and shifts right care from ER (level 4) to home self-care (level 1).
